It penalizes exit opacities that are neither fully opaque nor fully transparent, reducing the entropy of the exit opacities based on the intuition that most rays should strike the object or the background rather than grazing surfaces [S2].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S2]. The source explicitly states that the beta distribution prior (Beta(0.5, 0.5)) 'reduces the entropy of the exit opacities' and is based on the 'intuition that most of our rays should strike the object or the background'. The mathematical formulation provided in the source (negative log-likelihood of Beta(0.5, 0.5)) inherently penalizes values in the middle of the [0, 1] range (neither fully opaque nor fully transparent) because the Beta(0.5, 0.5) distribution has singularities at 0 and 1, effectively encouraging binary outcomes. Thus, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
